BiblicalUsage: Yâsham means to lie waste, to be desolate. Ezekiel warns that the cities shall be laid waste and the high places desolate, and the Egyptians begged Pharaoh for seed lest the land be desolate.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe desolation is the fruit of idolatry, and the land God gave can lie waste when His people forget Him.
